item.title: Borel's computation of the ranks of $K$-theory revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.26885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reprove Borel's computation of the rank of the $K$-groups of rings of algebraic integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ for certain number fields, e.g., $F = \mathbb{Q}(\mu_{l^k})$ for $l$ an odd regular prime number. The idea is to recover a simple formula for $l$-adic {\'e}tale cohomology groups of $\mathcal{O}_F$ in terms of Iwasawa theoretic objects without using Borel's result as an input.
item.dc:creator: Jan Ole Hesse

item.title: On the Motivic K-Theories of Classifying Spaces of Cyclic 2-Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the $2$-completed integral motivic homology, effective algebraic $K$-theory, and very effective Hermitian $K$-theory of the geometric classifying spaces $B\mu_{2^n}$, $n\geq 2$, over algebraically closed and real closed fields. We first carry out the corresponding classical calculations and, then obtain the motivic results using motivic spectral sequences and comparison techniques. The results reveal the classical $2$-torsion together with motivic $\tau$-periodicity and $\rho$-torsion.
item.dc:creator: Prerna Dhankhar

item.title: The integral $K_0$-ring of the stack of smooth hyperelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.27267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the integral $K_0$-ring of the moduli stack $\mathscr H_g$ of smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g\ge2$ over a field of characteristic zero. We show that it is a free abelian group of rank $8g+2$ for even $g$ and $8g+4$ for odd $g$. We use the isotypic decomposition of the $K_0$ of a related $\mu_{g+1}$-gerbe to obtain presentations for both even and odd $g$'s from the standard quotient presentation of $\mathscr H_g$. Thus, our technique differs from the $CH^\bullet(\mathscr H_g)$ computations of Edidin--Fulghesu, Fulghesu--Viviani, Di Lorenzo, and the $K_0(\mathscr M_2)$ computation of Edidin--Hu. Using Pagani's description of the inertia stack of $\mathscr H_g$, we apply Riemann--Roch to interpret the rank of $K_0(\mathscr H_g)$ as the number of inertia components. Finally, we compare the $K_0$ and Chow rings of $\mathscr H_g$ through the gamma-filtration and give presentations to the associated graded rings $\operatorname{gr}_{\gamma}K_0(\mathscr H_g)\otimes\mathbb F_p$ for every prime $p$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Ruofan Zeng

item.title: Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. These indices are the Euler characteristics of the corresponding $L^2$-cohomologies. This generalizes a result of J. Rosenberg for manifolds. The proof uses Witten deformation of the de Rham operator associated with a stratified Morse function, following the work of \'Alvarez L\'opez and Calaza.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadali Aligholi

item.title: Dold--Kan Correspondences via Morita Normalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.28138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical Dold--Kan correspondence identifies simplicial modules with connective chain complexes. Using Morita theory, we construct a Dold--Kan-type correspondence for every linear category carrying a suitable action of the maximum-preserving simplicial operators. The construction functorially assigns a Morita-equivalent normalized category to every such linear category. In particular, we obtain Dold--Kan-type correspondences for all crossed simplicial groups. We prove a rank formula for the normalized hom-modules and show that a crossed simplicial group is self-dual precisely when its underlying simplicial set of automorphism groups has dimension one. Furthermore, we construct normalization-compatible self-dualities and recover the Dwyer--Kan correspondence for duplicial, paracyclic and N-cyclic modules.
item.dc:creator: Florian Warg

item.title: Equivariant aspects of de-completing cyclic homology
item.description: arXiv:2410.05994v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Derived de Rham cohomology turns out to be important in $p$-adic geometry, following Bhatt's discovery [Bha12] of conjugate filtration in char $p$, de-Hodge-completing results in [Bei12]. In [Kal18], Kaledin introduced an analogous de-completion of the periodic cyclic homology, called the polynomial periodic cyclic homology, equipped with a conjugate filtration in char $p$, and expected to be related to derived de Rham cohomology. In this article, using genuine equivariant homotopy structure on Hochschild homology as in [ABG+18, BHM22], we give an equivariant description of Kaledin's polynomial periodic cyclic homology. This leads to Morita invariance without any Noetherianness assumption as in [Kal18], and the comparison to derived de Rham cohomology becomes transparent. Moreover, this description adapts directly to "topological" analogues, which gives rise to a de-Nygaard-completion of the topological periodic cyclic homology, which admits an extension to linear categories over truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. As an application, we establish a noncommutative crystalline--de Rham comparison, which decompletes the result in [PV19], and extends it to prime $p=2$. We also compare polynomial periodic cyclic homology to topological Hochschild homology over $\mathbb F_p$, and produce a conjugate filtration in char p from our description.
item.dc:creator: Zhouhang Mao

item.title: The span-squares adjunction
item.description: arXiv:2606.10052v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show a universal property of the span $\infty$-category that yields a description of functors defined on this category. For this, we view the span construction as a functor from double $\infty$-categories to $\infty$-categories, and show that this functor admits a right adjoint defined by the double $\infty$-categories of squares. As an application, we obtain a model for the localization of an $\infty$-category in terms of a span $\infty$-category and also give another proof of the model given by the relative nerve. Moreover, using the span-squares adjunction, we obtain new proofs of the equivalences between different models of algebraic $K$-theory, given by the $\Q$-, the $\oS$-, the cobordism model, and the squares construction.
item.dc:creator: George Raptis, Wolfgang Steimle
